title: stream-facade-lightweight-cred-fallback-and-backoff-profiles
author: Ethan Moore
release_notes: Introduce a lightweight streaming facade that unifies pull-style iterators across Go/TS/Python, adds a credential fallback mesh for short-lived tokens, and exposes configurable backoff profiles for ergonomic defaults.
description: Context and motivation: Multiple downstream teams reported friction when migrating from push-based stream handlers to more ergonomic pull-iterators and when rotating short-lived credentials in multi-tenant setups. This PR introduces a small, pluggable streaming facade (pull-iterator API) surfaced by the redwood runtime and SDK adapters, a credential-fallback mesh that lets SDKs fall back through a prioritized chain (env -> host-proxy -> refresh-token-provider) without surface changes to application code, and a set of named backoff profiles (fast/standard/steady) to simplify retry ergonomics. Checklist: - [x] Implement pull-style streaming facade in the runtime shim - [x] Add thin adapter implementations in go/ts/python SDK layers - [x] Credential fallback chain with clear opt-out - [x] Add named backoff profiles + telemetry hooks - [x] Update docs, examples, and changelog - [x] Cross-SDK integration tests and local e2e run Commits summary: commit 1: add streaming facade interface and initial runtime bridge; commit 2: implement credential fallback mesh and priority resolver; commit 3: add backoff profile registry and default policy; commit 4: SDK adapters (go/ts/python) and small portability shims; commit 5: tests, docs, and changelog updates. Changed areas/files (high level): - runtime/streaming/facade.go: new lightweight facade and interface adapters - runtime/auth/fallback_resolver.go: prioritized credential chain - sdk/go/adapter/pullstream.go: go-side adapter and examples - sdk/ts/src/pullIteratorAdapter.ts: typescript adapter + typed examples - sdk/python/redwood/pull_stream.py: python pull iterator shim - docs/sdk/streaming.md: design and migration guide - tests/integration/stream_pull_e2e: cross-sdk e2e harness Notable implementation details: the facade is intentionally minimal (Next()/peek token semantics) to avoid coupling to transport changes; the credential mesh resolves providers in order and only uses the next provider if the previous returns a 401 or expired-token sentinel; backoff profiles are parameterized (initial_ms, max_ms, multiplier, jitter) and registered centrally to ensure parity across SDKs. Review conversation highlights: - Sofia: "Can we avoid implicit blocking on Next() for sync SDKs?" Author reply: "The adapter exposes both async and sync wrappers; sync callers get a small bounded worker that buffers 1 item to avoid unbounded blocking." - Miguel: "Telemetry hooks need callsite labels for batching vs single-token flows." Author: "Added 'stream.kind' tag and unit tests." - Ava: "Do we risk credential leakage when proxying fallback providers?" Author: "The mesh enforces a single in-memory token cache per request scope and optionally emits audit events; documented and opt-outtable." CI and testing: initial CI run flagged lint failures in the TS adapter; those were fixed in commit 4. Integration matrix run passed across go1.21, node18, python3.11 matrices. Flaky test observed in e2e harness (stream termination race) and mitigated by adding a small grace window and idempotent close semantics. Performance and compatibility notes: microbenchmarks show the facade adds ~0.8-1.4% CPU overhead on steady throughput but simplifies caller code and avoids complex coroutine juggling. Compatibility layer ensures existing push-based streaming clients continue to work; new API is additive. Migration notes: documented step-by-step guide in docs/sdk/streaming.md and added small examples in sdk/*/examples/pullstream. Security and privacy: credential fallback respects KMS boundaries and never logs token material; audit events are opt-in. Release plan: included in next patch SDK release cycle; manual migration guidance and an automated codemod for TypeScript added under tools/codemods. Merge outcome: PR was approved by all reviewers and merged via squash on 2026-03-04 after green CI. Related work: follows up on ENG-7541 (stream ergonomics spike) and pairs with a future runtime scheduling change (ENG-9620).
